title: Simultaneous Linear Equations
subtitle: A system of simultaneous equations means several equations that must all be satisfied at the same time. The key skill this week: writing any system as the matrix equation AX = C, and building the augmented matrix [A|C] you'll need for every elimination method.

topics.title: Writing a System as AX = C

subtopics.title: Writing a System as AX = C

content.text: Pull the coefficients into matrix A, the unknowns into column vector X, and the right-hand side into column vector C. Then append C to A to form the augmented matrix — this is the only thing you write when starting any elimination method.
2019/2020 Q1c — Build the augmented matrix
01
The system
i₁ + 3i₂ - 2i₃ = 6 ... (equation 1) 4i₁ + 5i₂ + 2i₃ = 3 ... (equation 2) i₁ + 3i₂ + 4i₃ = 7 ... (equation 3)
02
Extract coefficient matrix A — coefficients only, no constants
i₁ i₂ i₃ A = [ 1 3 -2 ] ← eq 1 [ 4 5 2 ] ← eq 2 [ 1 3 4 ] ← eq 3
03
Build augmented matrix [A | C] — append the RHS constants
The vertical bar is just notation. Everything to its left came from A; everything to its right came from C.

Common mistake — Starting row operations on just A without the constants column. Every operation you do must be applied to the full row including the augmented column — otherwise your final answers will be wrong.
Exam focus:

items: Form A and A_b for: i₁+3i₂−2i₃=6, 4i₁+5i₂+2i₃=3, i₁+3i₂+4i₃=7. Find ranks and nature of solution. (2019/2020 Q1c, 12 marks)
State conditions for (i) no solution (ii) infinite solutions (iii) unique solution. (2019/2020 Q1b, 5 marks)

content.text: Before solving, you can already tell what kind of solution you'll get just by comparing the ranks of A and [A|C].

Solution Conditions — based on Rank
Unique solution
rank(A) = rank([A|C]) = n (n = number of unknowns). Lines cross at one point.
No solution
rank([A|C]) > rank(A). System is inconsistent — equations contradict each other. Parallel lines.
Infinite solutions
rank(A) = rank([A|C]) n. Equations are not fully independent. Same line (one is a multiple of another).
2019/2020 Q1c — Determine nature of solution using rank
01
Row reduce A to find rank(A)
02
Apply same operations to [A|C] to find rank([A|C])
03
Compare and conclude
rank(A) = 3 rank([A|C]) = 3 n = 3 (unknowns: i₁, i₂, i₃) rank(A) = rank([A|C]) = n = 3
∴ UNIQUE SOLUTION — the system has exactly one answer
2019/2020 Q1c is 12 marks. Correctly forming [A|C] and finding both ranks earns partial credit even if you don't solve the full system.

content.text: These are the only operations you're allowed to do to a matrix. They don't change the solution — they just reorganise how the equations are written. Every Gaussian and Gauss-Jordan step is one of these three.

Three Permissible Operations
Rᵢ ↔ Rⱼ
Swap rows i and j. The order of equations doesn't affect the solution.
Rᵢ → k · Rᵢ
Multiply every entry in row i by a non-zero constant k. k must be non-zero — multiplying by 0 destroys the equation.
Rᵢ → Rᵢ + k · Rⱼ
Add k times row j to every entry in row i. This is how you create zeros in specific columns.

Common mistake — When doing R₂ → R₂ + k·R₁ , applying it to only the first few columns and forgetting the augmented constants column. Every entry in the row — including the constant after the vertical bar — must be updated.
